clusters.name: Angles, radian measure, and the unit circle

standards.description: Guide students to convert between degree and radian measure and use both systems to describe angles in standard position.
standards.ccssText: Convert between degree and radian measure; define angles in standard position, coterminal angles, and arc length; apply both units in geometric and real-world contexts.

standards.description: Help students define the unit circle and use it to evaluate all six trigonometric functions at standard angles.
standards.ccssText: Define and use the unit circle to evaluate trigonometric functions at standard angles (multiples of 30° and 45°); identify coordinates and exact values for sine, cosine, and tangent.

standards.description: Extend trigonometric function definitions to all angles by using reference angles and the sign conventions of each quadrant.
standards.ccssText: Extend trigonometric functions to all angles using reference angles and the signs of functions in each quadrant; evaluate trig functions for non-standard angles using a calculator.

standards.description: Help students graph sine, cosine, tangent, and their transformations, identifying amplitude, period, phase shift, and midline from equations and graphs.
standards.ccssText: Graph sine, cosine, tangent, and their transformations; identify and interpret amplitude, period, phase shift, and midline; write equations from graphs of transformed trig functions.

standards.description: Define, graph, and evaluate inverse trigonometric functions, helping students understand why domain restrictions are necessary.
standards.ccssText: Define inverse trigonometric functions (arcsin, arccos, arctan) by restricting domains; graph each inverse; evaluate exact and approximate values; compose trig and inverse trig functions.

standards.description: Guide students to verify identities and apply fundamental, sum/difference, double-angle, and half-angle formulas to simplify and evaluate expressions.
standards.ccssText: Verify and apply fundamental trigonometric identities (Pythagorean, quotient, reciprocal), sum and difference formulas, double-angle formulas, and half-angle formulas.

standards.description: Teach students to solve trigonometric equations algebraically and graphically over specified intervals, including those requiring the use of identities.
standards.ccssText: Solve trigonometric equations algebraically and graphically over specified intervals; identify general solutions; use identities to simplify equations before solving.

standards.description: Apply the Law of Sines to solve oblique triangles, guiding students through the ambiguous (SSA) case and its possible outcomes.
standards.ccssText: Apply the Law of Sines to solve oblique triangles; analyze the ambiguous (SSA) case and determine whether zero, one, or two triangles are determined; compute triangle area using (1/2)ab sin C.

standards.description: Apply the Law of Cosines to solve oblique triangles and find area using Heron's formula when no angle is known.
standards.ccssText: Apply the Law of Cosines to solve oblique triangles (SAS and SSS cases); derive and use Heron's formula for the area of a triangle given three sides.

standards.description: Help students describe the end behavior of polynomial functions using degree and leading coefficient and connect this to graphical analysis.
standards.ccssText: Describe the end behavior of polynomial functions using degree and leading coefficient; distinguish even- and odd-degree polynomials; sketch graphs consistent with end behavior and zeros.

standards.description: Guide students to find real and complex zeros of polynomial functions using factoring, synthetic division, and the Rational Root Theorem.
standards.ccssText: Find real and complex zeros of polynomial functions using factoring, synthetic division, the Rational Root Theorem, and the Conjugate Pairs Theorem; apply the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra.

standards.description: Teach students to identify asymptotes, graph rational functions, and solve rational equations and inequalities by analyzing numerator and denominator structure.
standards.ccssText: Identify vertical, horizontal, and oblique asymptotes of rational functions; graph rational functions including holes; solve rational equations and inequalities; interpret behavior near asymptotes.

standards.description: Help students graph exponential functions, identify growth and decay, and apply compound interest and continuous growth formulas involving e.
standards.ccssText: Graph and transform exponential functions; classify as growth or decay; apply compound interest (A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt)) and continuous growth (A = Pe^(rt)) formulas.

standards.description: Define logarithms as inverses of exponentials, teach the change-of-base formula, and graph logarithmic functions and their transformations.
standards.ccssText: Define logarithms as inverses of exponential functions; apply the change-of-base formula; graph logarithmic functions and identify transformations, domain, range, and asymptotes.

standards.description: Apply product, quotient, and power properties of logarithms to simplify expressions and solve exponential and logarithmic equations.
standards.ccssText: Apply product, quotient, and power rules for logarithms to expand and condense expressions; solve exponential and logarithmic equations algebraically; check for extraneous solutions.

standards.description: Derive and apply the standard equation of a parabola, helping students identify the focus, directrix, vertex, and axis of symmetry.
standards.ccssText: Derive the standard-form equation of a parabola from the focus-directrix definition; identify and locate vertex, focus, directrix, and axis of symmetry; graph parabolas in standard and general form.

standards.description: Guide students to derive and apply the standard equation of an ellipse, identifying foci, vertices, co-vertices, and axes of symmetry.
standards.ccssText: Derive the standard-form equation of an ellipse from the definition involving two foci; identify center, foci, vertices, and co-vertices; graph horizontal and vertical ellipses.

standards.description: Teach students to derive and apply the standard equation of a hyperbola, identifying foci, vertices, and asymptotes.
standards.ccssText: Derive the standard-form equation of a hyperbola; identify center, foci, vertices, and asymptotes; sketch hyperbolas; distinguish horizontal and vertical orientations.

standards.description: Help students convert between polar and rectangular coordinates and graph polar equations, recognizing common curves such as limacons, rose curves, and cardioids.
standards.ccssText: Convert between polar and rectangular coordinate forms; graph polar equations including circles, limacons, rose curves, and cardioids; convert equations between polar and rectangular form.

standards.description: Help students identify arithmetic sequences and derive and apply formulas for the nth term and partial sums.
standards.ccssText: Identify arithmetic sequences by common difference; derive and apply formulas for the nth term (a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d) and the partial sum (S_n = n(a_1 + a_n)/2); apply to real-world contexts.

standards.description: Guide students to identify geometric sequences and apply formulas for the nth term, partial sums, and infinite series convergence.
standards.ccssText: Identify geometric sequences by common ratio; derive and apply formulas for the nth term (a_n = a_1·r^(n-1)), partial sums, and the sum of a convergent infinite geometric series (S = a_1/(1-r) for |r| < 1).

standards.description: Introduce the informal concept of a limit and help students evaluate limits graphically and numerically, identifying cases where the limit does not exist.
standards.ccssText: Understand the informal concept of a limit as a function value approached but not necessarily reached; evaluate limits graphically and numerically; identify cases of non-existence (oscillation, unbounded behavior, one-sided disagreement).

standards.description: Help students represent vectors geometrically and in component form, performing addition, subtraction, and scalar multiplication.
standards.ccssText: Represent vectors geometrically as directed line segments and in component form (a, b); perform vector addition, subtraction, and scalar multiplication; find magnitude and direction angle.

standards.description: Teach students to compute the dot product, find the angle between two vectors, and determine orthogonality.
standards.ccssText: Compute the dot product of two vectors; use the dot product to find the angle between vectors and to determine whether vectors are orthogonal; find vector projections.

standards.description: Define and graph parametric curves, guide students to eliminate the parameter to find a rectangular equation, and apply to projectile motion.
standards.ccssText: Define and graph parametric curves in the plane; eliminate the parameter to obtain a rectangular equation; apply parametric equations to model projectile motion and other real-world scenarios.
